claim: Logic and control are separable: the same Horn clauses give the same meaning under top-down or bottom-up control; control changes only efficiency. This is the origin of rules as a checkable form.
agent_test: Write a task's rules once as declarative clauses; run two control orders (forward, backward) and check the answers agree, at equal tokens.

claim: Negation as failure and stable-model semantics make logic programs non-monotonic: adding a fact can remove a conclusion, and a program can have zero, one or many answer sets. Primary papers were not opened (from memory).
agent_test: Add a late fact to a rule base and check the agent retracts the conclusion rather than keeping it.

claim: Expressive power costs tractability: SHIQ with unrestricted role inclusions is undecidable (opened). The general Brachman-Levesque tradeoff and DL handbook claims were not opened.
agent_test: Constrain the rule language the agent writes in S2 to a decidable fragment and compare time-outs against free-form FOL.

claim: Translate-then-solve (LLM writes a logic, constraint, ASP or Prolog program, a solver answers) beats standard prompting and CoT on multi-step, constraint-heavy or relational tasks across at least six independent papers.
agent_test: On constraint and multi-hop items, route to a solver arm vs a CoT arm at equal tokens; count wins by depth.

claim: The solver route is not uniformly better. Where CoT already does forward chaining on easy synthetic sets, CoT matches or beats it: GPT-4 PrOntoQA CoT 98.79 vs Logic-LM 83.20; ChatGPT PrOntoQA CoT 67.80 vs Logic-LM 61.00; GPT-4 FOLIO CoT 75.3 vs LINC 72.5 (p=0.58); ProverQA-paper ProntoQA CoT 100.0 for GPT-4o.
agent_test: Gate the solver route: plain CoT for shallow short-chain items; measure tokens saved.

claim: The bottleneck moves from reasoning to formalising. Programs run almost always on synthetic data (PrOntoQA 100%, ProofWriter 99.0% executable) but rarely on exam text (FOLIO 79.9%, AR-LSAT 32.6%). Small models make 38% (StarCoder+) FOL syntax errors; weak parsers lose most of the gain; DL wording drops a fine-tuned model to 58.5%; one-shot ASP is often semantically wrong though it parses.
agent_test: Measure round-trip fidelity: translate NL to rules, back-translate, compare; correlate with final accuracy.

claim: Solver error messages repair syntax but not meaning: executable rate +5.01 points on average, yet FOLIO GPT-4 accuracy on executable items goes 80.4 to 79.9. Logic-LM++ shows plain refinement can add a semantic error, and gains about 5% from an LLM pairwise comparison step.
agent_test: Compare refinement on error text only vs refinement plus an independent semantic check, at equal tokens.

claim: The gain comes from the solver, not from writing a formal spec: SatLM with the solver removed (SatNoSolver) scores 26.6/23.7/40.7 on GSM-SYS/GSM/CLUTRR vs standard 21.0/22.2/41.2. LINC's scratchpad (formulae, no prover) did not beat naive prompting.
agent_test: Ablate: formal spec written but answered by CoT vs spec executed; expect the first to match plain prompting.

claim: A solver returns more than a crash: UNSAT (rules conflict) and AMBIG (underdetermined). Abstaining on these lifts selective accuracy: SatLM 77% vs program-aided 45% on GSM-SYS. LINC precision on True/False is 93% vs CoT 81%, at lower recall (60% vs 75%) because it says Uncertain 57% of the time.
agent_test: Add UNSAT and AMBIG as explicit states; measure selective accuracy and coverage.

claim: The solver advantage grows with depth and variable interdependence: Logic-LM minus CoT is +7.1, +5.0, +12.7, +20.0, +39.4 points at ProofWriter depth 0,1,2,4,5. Text-only GPT-4 falls from 100% to 0% as interdependence goes 1 to 4 while Prolog stays stable. StarCoder+ baselines stay near chance with depth while LINC stays far above.
agent_test: Stratify items by depth; plot solver-arm minus CoT-arm gain against depth.

claim: Declarative targets (constraints, Prolog, ASP) beat imperative code when the problem is constraint-heavy: SatLM GSM-SYS 69.4 vs program-aided 43.4, but equal on plain GSM greedy (71.8 vs 72.7).
agent_test: Choose target form per item type: declarative for constraint items, code for sequential arithmetic.

claim: LLMs take valid single deduction steps but fail at proof planning: in PrOntoQA 5-hop fictional ontology 93.2% of steps were strictly valid, but with several steps open they pick a misleading one. SatLM's CoT-solver error split agrees: 72.5% planning errors on GSM-SYS.
agent_test: Give the agent an explicit search and backtracking operator over candidate inferences; measure misleading-step rate.

claim: Prior world knowledge props up rule reasoning: accuracy is clearly higher with true ontologies than fictional or false ones (exact values only in a figure).
agent_test: Test rule reasoning on counterfactual versions of each rule base to separate retrieval from deduction.

claim: Models trained on synthetic rule text reason over rules in language and generalise to deeper chains: RuleTaker about 99% in distribution, D3-trained 97.6% at depth 5, D2-trained 71.1% at depth 3, 81% of expected true-to-false flips when a critical sentence is removed (16654/20549); ProofWriter proof accuracy +9 absolute; fine-tuned DeBERTa 97.5% on ALCQ.
agent_test: Use as an upper reference only; our agent is not trained.

claim: Whether formal wording hurts is contested: a fine-tuned DeBERTa falls from 95.3% (meaningless names) to 58.5% (DL terms), but OWL-proof tests find formal vs natural form costs under 8% and logical complexity matters more. Gap search: in prompted models, enumerated predicate names (No-C.) scored 45.49 vs 58.42 for meaningful names (Beiser et al., 6 LLMs, ProntoQA and ProofWriter), a 13-point drop, so naming matters at least for translation.
agent_test: Present the same rules in natural and formal wording to the agent; compare accuracy.

claim: Description-logic and ontology reasoning is hard for LLMs: OntoURL SWRL and DL reasoning 60-75% (Qwen2.5-72B DL 68.4, 3B 51.1 on a 50% chance), ontology construction near 0-22; DL-Lite performance drops toward 0 beyond an ABox size threshold; GPT-4 ALCQ 9-shot 77-89 and 0-shot 30-42 on a 33% chance.
agent_test: Keep large fact lists out of the prompt; store facts externally and fetch.

claim: Noise and missing premises degrade ontology proof tasks: up to 47% drop in extraction with 1:20 irrelevant axioms and up to 38% with missing premises (OWL EL, few ontologies).
agent_test: Test rule retrieval: only relevant rules vs rules plus distractors at equal tokens.

claim: CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic tasks and even there a solver beats it. On FOLIO, CoT vs direct for GPT-4o is 79.8 vs 62.6 but Gemini 1.5 Pro 73.9 vs 74.4, so the CoT gain is model-dependent (column order now confirmed: Table 7 header lists zero-shot CoT accuracy before direct answer; still 2024 non-reasoning models).
agent_test: Do not assume CoT helps on logic items; route by task type.

claim: An agent loop with solver feedback can saturate ASP generation (ASP-Bench: Claude Sonnet 4.5 solved all 128 problems in every run, mean 7.7 solver calls on hard), while one-shot generation is semantically poor (BLAST syntax 0.6-1.0, semantic often 0-0.4; 17 of 21 graph problems flawed earlier). Loop vs one-shot and benchmark artefacts are not separated.
agent_test: Run one-shot vs tool-loop on the same rule-writing items with test-suite scoring.

claim: A reusable hand-written knowledge module plus an LLM fact parser gives near-perfect results (bAbI 99.99 vs CoT 86.18) and exposes benchmark label errors (about 10.7% of StepGame labels; 16 of 400 CLUTRR items), but needs modules per domain and a good parser.
agent_test: Keep a small library of verified rule modules (time, space, kinship) the agent reuses.

claim: Faithful-by-construction chains: the solver answer follows from the written chain. Beats CoT on 9 of 10 benchmarks (relative MWP +6.3, CLUTRR +21.4) but gives no gain on StrategyQA and Sports where knowledge retrieval is the hard part.
agent_test: Check that the final answer changes when the written chain is edited.

claim: Retrieval of knowledge is a separate bottleneck: Lyu's StrategyQA result, Cyc's decades of hand-written axioms, and Think-on-Graph's need for a well-formed graph (GPT-4 CWQ Hits@1 67.6, WebQSP 82.6; below fine-tuned on Simple Questions) all point to facts, not reasoning.
agent_test: Test fact grounding separately from rule execution; log which fails.

claim: LINC and CoT fail on different items (mistake overlap 0.14-0.22 vs 0.52-0.56 among CoT variants), so combining should help, but no ensemble was tested in the paper. Gap search: a related hybrid (NSCoT, CoT then FOL) still trailed CoT on FOLIO for 5 open models, but it is a pipeline, not an agreement ensemble.
agent_test: Run solver arm and CoT arm; accept on agreement, escalate on disagreement; compare with either alone.

claim: FOLIO GPT-4 results conflict across papers: Logic-LM 78.9 vs CoT 70.6, Logic-LM++ 84.8, LINC 72.5 vs CoT 75.3. Likely causes: CoT fallback for 20.1% non-executable items, 10-vote majority, different prompts and subsets. Not resolved.
agent_test: Replicate both pipelines on one FOLIO split with identical token budgets.

claim: Older benchmarks overstate ability: GPT-4o CoT on ProverQA is 94.2/79.4/50.0 (easy/medium/hard), Claude-3.5-Sonnet 95.2/83.6/56.4, while ProntoQA is 100 and 99.2. No solver arm was tested on the hard split. Gap search: the ProverQA paper text does not state the label mix, so 'near chance' for hard (33.3% for a balanced 3-way label) stays unverified; no solver arm was run there.
agent_test: Evaluate the schema on ProverQA hard with a solver arm at equal tokens.

claim: Solver routes beat CoT mainly on search-heavy constraint problems, and CoT wins on shallow deduction and implicit-rule items. GPT-4o: ZebraLogic avg CoT 28.2 vs declarative Prolog 58.8 and Python 71.7; EntailmentBank CoT 81.8 far above Prolog. On FOLIO with open models CoT beats LINC for all five (e.g. Qwen2.5-32B 75.49 vs 68.14).
agent_test: Gate by constraint-search structure; run CoT on shallow items.

claim: With 2025 reasoning models the solver route still adds a lot on hard constraint tasks: mean accuracy 51.3 to 78.0 over seven task columns; o4-mini 63.4 to 82.3, DeepSeek-R1 52.3 to 81.9, Gemini 2.5 Pro 62.9 to 93.9; ZL-XXL 24.2 to 71.3. No FOLIO, ProverQA or AR-LSAT arm exists for these models.
agent_test: Run a reasoning-model CoT arm against a solver arm on FOLIO, ProverQA hard and AR-LSAT at equal tokens.

claim: Translate-and-solve cost is dominated by retries and repair rounds: mean 2.18 revisions (Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.45, DeepSeek-V3 5.43), 7.7 agent tool calls on hard ASP items (up to 26; one item about 622k input tokens), 6 to 26 LLM calls per repair in round-trip repair. On 12x12 Zebra the solver arm matched the baseline's token use (about 25k) and got 100% vs 0%. A full token-per-correct comparison with CoT on logic benchmarks is still missing.
agent_test: Log LLM calls and tokens per item for solver and CoT arms; report tokens per correct answer.

claim: The model that wrote the program is a weak judge of it: after solver feedback, the LLM approves wrong outputs 5.06% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) to 37.33% (DeepSeek-V3) of the time; o4-mini 12.42%, R1 13.86%. Self-approval breaks G5 for weaker models.
agent_test: Replace self-approval with an independent check (round trip, tests, second translator) and measure false accepts.

claim: A solver-checked round trip (formalise, back-translate, re-formalise, test equivalence) needs no gold label and tracks faithfulness: 85.3% of Traffic rules equivalent after diagnosis-guided repair vs 44.7% before; unfaithful or minor on 7% of equivalent vs 27% of non-equivalent rules (25-rule human check by one author). It misses some errors and costs 3 translations per item. No comparison with test cases or a second translator.
agent_test: Add a round-trip equivalence test and a small test-case set; compare false-accept and cost.

claim: The rule fragment matters for defaults. SMT is better on plain puzzles (ZL-XL 84.0 vs 75.2) but collapses on default and exception tasks (MultiLogicNMR skeptical 35.8 vs ASP 92.9; chance 33.3), below the LLM alone. Models mix strong and default negation in ASP. Datalog, Horn and decidable DL fragments have not been compared at all.
agent_test: Use ASP when rules have exceptions; add a short target-language guide (compact 73.1 vs none 61.4).

claim: Frontier models handle explicit defeasible rules without a solver: BoardgameQA ASP 82.4 vs baseline 84.7 (reasoning models 92.0 vs 88.0). The ASP gain appears only when the answer depends on comparing several consistent worlds (credulous 81.0 vs 52.9). Implicit rules and missing facts are lost in translation, as with EntailmentBank where Prolog is far below CoT.
agent_test: Test open-ended items with missing facts; require a step that lists implicit rules before translation.

claim: Routing evidence is thin: a BERT classifier picks the needed inference type with 92.6% accuracy, but no gate for solver vs CoT based on depth, interdependence or constraint count has been tested. The only supported rule is the He and Wang pattern (search-heavy yes, shallow no).
agent_test: Fit a router on cheap text features and test it against always-solver and always-CoT.
